subject: URG: Riverbank throughput blackout — request to geo-redispatch and exec comms
messages:
From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@riverbank.health>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, ops@riverbank.health
Date: Thu, 3 Oct 2029 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Immediate: API throughput blackhole in us-west-2

Olga / Redwood team —

We started seeing a dramatic drop in successful inference throughput at ~14:45 UTC for our production endpoints (all traffic pin: us-west-2). Error rate jumped from 0.6% -> 22% and median latency increased from 140ms -> 2.4s. Customers are seeing timeouts. We have 3 downstream services failing health checks.

We pulled logs and there are a lot of 504s from the gateway and token generation failures on your side (see attached minimal export). Can you confirm this is not an agent within our stack and advise immediate mitigation steps? We need an ETA for stabilization and whether you can reroute traffic to another region now. This is P0 for Riverbank.

-Paul
SRE, Riverbank Health

Attachments: riverbank_metrics_08-12-UTC.json (application/json, 280 KB)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@riverbank.health>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Oct 2029 15:22:46 +0000
Subject: Re: Immediate: API throughput blackhole in us-west-2

Paul — thanks for the quick heads-up and the export, I’m on it.

Initial triage: our telemetry shows a sudden tail QPS increase on Riverbank's primary model route at 14:42 UTC that caused the us-west-2 pool for your Dedicated capacity to hit a sustained queue length and trigger request throttling. We are seeing corresponding 502/504s from the edge towards the serving pool.

What I’m doing now:
- Opening an internal P0 bridge and pulling the cluster metrics (in-flight requests, KV cache pressure, batch latency)
- Preparing an emergency geo-redispatch to push traffic to us-east-1 if we confirm model compatibility and KV cache cold-start window is acceptable
- Notifying our on-call infra lead and requesting temporary priority scaling for your pool

Can you pause non-essential batch jobs on your side and confirm whether you accept a geo-redispatch to us-east-1 for up to 2 hours while we heal the primary pool?

I’ll loop back in 10m with an update.

—Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Oct 2029 15:28:05 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Immediate: API throughput blackhole in us-west-2

Forwarding Riverbank's alert. Key notes from infra console: us-west-2 GPU pool for RB-PRIME is at 98% allocation, one host reporting OOM events but not machine-wide. Autoscaler attempted a scale but was blocked by regional capacity quota for our Dedicated tenancy. We have two options:

1) Approve geo-redispatch to us-east-1 now (hot swap traffic, expect ~60s of elevated latency while KV warming).
2) Request emergency burst capacity quota from cloud partner (likely 6–12m to approve).

I recommend (1) to get customer stable immediately and then follow up on capacity. Marcus — can you prepare the runbook to trigger redispatch and rollback? Hannah — prep exec note for Riverbank C-suite and Legal (they asked for communications). Rishi — we may need a small account credit; can you surface precedents?

-Vanessa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Team —
Confirmed: model binary is compatible across regions and we have a validated quantized variant in us-east-1. Runbook drafted (attached) includes the exact command set for the controller to switch the routing policy to "geo-redispatch" for Riverbank's primary endpoints, TTL for KV replication, and monitoring checks. Estimated customer-visible stabilization: 2–3 minutes for initial traffic shift, 40–90s for per-request latency spike while caches warm, then back to normal.

I will lead the operator execution. Marcus, I need a signed approval from an exec on the temporary rollback credit and a comms plan for Riverbank's CTO.

-Hannah
Director, Applied Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook_emergency_redispatch.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Oct 2029 15:43:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Immediate: API throughput blackhole in us-west-2

Vanessa / Olga —
I approve an immediate geo-redispatch to us-east-1. Given the impact window and Riverbank's enterprise SLA, propose the following:

- Execute geo-redispatch now (max 2 hours)
- Offer Riverbank a one-time 15% service credit for the hour of degraded experience and expedited postmortem with targeted mitigations (KV replication and autoscaler tuning)
- Notify AWS rep Amanda Cole to request short-term quota relief in us-west-2 while we repair the pool (Amanda looped).

Please prepare the external comms — succinct timeline & what we are doing. Olga, coordinate final message to Riverbank.

—Rishi
VP, Customer Success & Sales, Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Hart <emma.hart@riverbank.health>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@riverbank.health>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, amanda.cole@aws-partners.com
Date: Thu, 3 Oct 2029 15:48:30 +0000
Subject: Re: Immediate: API throughput blackhole in us-west-2 — action & timeline

Emma / Paul —
Thanks for flagging. We will execute an emergency geo-redispatch of your production endpoints from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 immediately. What to expect:

- Start now (T=0): controller will begin shifting session affinity; expect a brief increase in per-request latency for ~60–90s as KV caches warm.
- T+3m: majority of traffic served from us-east-1, error rate should drop to baseline.
- T+10m: confirm stable and begin gradual reintegration of us-west-2 after we repair the pool.

We are attaching the runbook and a short SLA snapshot. We will follow with an exec note for your leadership and a postmortem within 48h.

Do you want us to include a customer-facing status blurb for your site? Also, we’ll need your confirmation you’re comfortable with the temporary geo-redispatch and the proposed 15% credit window.

—Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: runbook_emergency_redispatch.pdf, sla_snapshot_q3.csv
